# Citation

Su, M., Pan, T., Chen, Q.-Z., Zhou, W.-W., Gong, Y., Xu, G., Yan, H.-Y., Li, S., Shi, Q.-Z., Zhang, Y., He, X., Jiang, C.-J., Fan, S.-C., Li, X., Cairns, M. J., Wang, X., and Li, Y.-S. (2022). Data analysis guidelines for single-cell RNA-seq in biomedical studies and clinical applications. *Military Medical Research* 9, 68. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40779-022-00434-8 (PDF p. 1).

# One-Sentence Summary

This review outlines experimental design, raw-data processing, standard scRNA-seq analysis and question-specific advanced analyses, and provides example scripts through an associated repository (PDF pp. 1–2, 14).

# Research Question

How should researchers design and analyze biomedical scRNA-seq studies from sequencing reads through cell annotation and advanced biological interpretation? This paraphrases the abstract and workflow overview (PDF pp. 1–3).

# Biological System

Biomedical single-cell studies, including disease and clinical samples used as examples; the review does not recruit a single new sample cohort or define one species-specific experiment (PDF pp. 1–3, Background and Experiment design).

# Study Design

Methodological review and guideline article, with a workflow divided into experimental design, preprocessing, basic analysis, and advanced tasks; published studies and tools supply its evidence (PDF pp. 1–3, 10–17). A new controlled benchmark across every listed tool or original patient cohort: Not reported.

# Data

Conceptual data are raw reads, barcode/UMI count matrices, patient or condition labels, reference annotations, and sometimes spatial or other omics information (PDF pp. 2–5, 8, 10–14). The article provides a supplementary tool list and a public repository of example software/scripts, but no single new study-wide raw count matrix is specified (PDF p. 14, “Software and analysis scripts”; p. 17, Supplementary Information).

# Methods

- Discuss case–control design, biological replicates, batch effects, raw read processing, cell QC and doublet removal (PDF pp. 2–4, “Experiment design” and “QC and doublet removal”).
- Survey normalization, integration, highly variable gene selection, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and annotation (PDF pp. 4–9, Figures 1–2).
- Survey trajectory inference/RNA velocity, ligand–receptor communication, regulons/TF activity and metabolic analysis (PDF pp. 10–15, Figures 3–5).
- Distinguish routine from question-dependent advanced analysis rather than applying all methods to every data set (PDF pp. 2, 15–17).

# Software and Versions

Discussed packages include Cell Ranger, Seurat, Scrublet, DoubletFinder, SCTransform, Scanorama, SC3, SingleR, NicheNet and scMetabolism (PDF pp. 3–8, 11–14). **CellPhoneDB version 4** is explicitly named in the communication discussion (PDF p. 10). Versions of a single unified software environment used for all examples: Not reported. The authors supply example scripts and environment guidance at https://github.com/WXlab-NJMU/scrna-recom (PDF pp. 2, 14); that repository's current contents are not assessed here.

# Important Parameters

No universal minimum UMI count, mitochondrial fraction, doublet-score cutoff, number of principal components or clustering resolution is reported for all experiments; the authors discuss context-dependent QC and analysis (PDF pp. 3–7). A cited ligand–receptor analysis uses **log2(FPKM) ≥ 5** for both genes; this is an **example from Camp et al.**, not a threshold endorsed across tools (PDF p. 11, “Cell–cell communications”).

# Inputs and Outputs

Inputs are raw sequencing data, experimental metadata and appropriate reference/knowledge resources; typical outputs are filtered expression matrices, clusters and labels, trajectories, inferred interaction scores and regulatory or metabolic summaries (PDF pp. 2–3, 7–15, Figures 1–5). These are conceptual outputs of reviewed methods; a shared output bundle for an original experiment: Not reported.

# Main Results

The authors present an organized workflow and cautions about poor-quality cells, doublets, batch effects and reference-dependent annotation (PDF pp. 2–9). They summarize advanced approaches to trajectories, communication, regulation and metabolism, and offer example scripts (PDF pp. 10–15). These are **guideline synthesis and interpretations of cited studies**, not new head-to-head performance estimates.

# Assumptions

Case–control differences must be considered alongside patient-level covariates and possible technical batches (PDF pp. 3–5). Cell annotation relies on adequate marker or reference information, and ligand–receptor scores infer interaction *potential* from expression rather than directly observing signaling (PDF pp. 7–9, 10–12).

# Limitations

The authors note that damaged cells complicate barcode thresholds, doublets distort clustering and expression analysis, and computational methods have context-dependent strengths (PDF pp. 3–4, 7, 15–16). They explicitly say that the online analysis pipeline cannot include all popular tools (PDF p. 14, “Software and analysis scripts”). The article is not a validation study for every tool it names.

# Reproducible Implementation Details

The paper points to scripts and environment guidance at https://github.com/WXlab-NJMU/scrna-recom and a supplementary tool table (PDF pp. 2, 14, 17). The PDF itself does not report one pinned commit, a uniform version lockfile, fixed seed, or single end-to-end configuration for all modalities: Not reported. To reproduce a specific cited result, its original study and precise dataset are required (**summary inference** from PDF pp. 2–17).

# Relevance to simitall

**Inference, not an author recommendation:** This guideline might serve as a source index if simitall includes scRNA-seq analysis topics. The authors do not mention or test simitall (PDF pp. 1–17).

# Terminology

- **UMI:** Unique molecular identifier used in single-cell count processing (PDF pp. 3–4).
- **Doublet:** Barcode containing material from more than one cell, potentially distorting cell analyses (PDF pp. 3–4).
- **RNA velocity:** Inference of expression dynamics from spliced and unspliced transcripts (PDF p. 10).
- **CCC:** Cell–cell communication inferred from patterns such as ligand–receptor expression (PDF pp. 10–12, Figure 3).

# References

Primary source: Su et al. (2022), cited above. Its original method and application studies appear in the References beginning on PDF p. 18. No outside sources were used.
